description: Discriminator: in the owner-alive case, does a legal single-NONE Commit for the owner's instance leave the admitted operation pending nowhere, or is it re-proposed onto the propose channel? Prefix: the harness admits the operation with the real handlePropose (which attaches it and broadcasts the PreAccept) and then delivers the commit to the real handleCommit. Controls: the same events print whether bookkeeping and a pending proposal existed before the commit, the instance status after it, the remaining pending count and the number of proposals on the channel.

harness.description: In-package Go test that admits one proposal with the real handler and delivers one legal NOOP commit, reporting the pending counts and the propose channel.
semantic_changes: harness-only scaffolding: the Replica is constructed in-package with buffer peer writers and the two handlers are called directly; the handlers are unmodified
the commit is delivered directly instead of through the run loop, so only the handler's effect on the proposal is observed

legality.derivation: Both steps are the protocol's own: handlePropose is what admits a client operation and the commit is what a recoverer broadcasts for a NOOP instance.
legality.applicability: One instance, one admitted operation, one commit.
unresolved: the run loop's later handling of the re-proposed proposal is not driven

grounding.derivation: The event reports the instance status after the commit, the remaining pending proposals and the proposals waiting on the channel, which together say whether the operation was re-proposed.
grounding.applicability: The owner held the admitted proposal and the commit was for its own instance.

observable_properties.description: After the owner processes a NOOP commit for an instance holding its admitted operation, the operation must be waiting on the propose channel.

uncertainties: the check covers the owner-alive case only; the restarted-owner case is claim C4's crash
the later commit and execution of the re-proposed operation are not driven, so the client's reply is not observed
